title: 4.6 A 0.8V, 31ppm/°C, -40dB DC-to-GHz Power-Supply-Rejection Standard-Vth Core-MOS-Only Voltage Reference with a 294µm2Area
problem: PVT-independent voltage references at sub-1V core-supply operation face headroom limitations from BJT V_EB and current-source saturation voltage; existing approaches require DNW base structures (non-standard CMOS) or switching-mode ripple filters (large area).
motivation: Advanced nodes demand core-device-only references for data converters and sensors operating at low core supply voltages with minimal area overhead and high reliability.
method: This design creates a stable voltage reference that works at just 0.8V power supply—a challenge because traditional approaches using BJTs (bipolar transistors) need significant voltage overhead to function, and existing solutions required either special non-standard transistor structures or large filtering circuits. Instead, it uses charge-pump and switched-capacitor circuits (transistor-based switching techniques that manage voltage with minimal overhead rather than pushing steady current through components). The result is exceptional: the voltage drifts only 31 parts per million per degree Celsius as temperature changes, and it rejects power-supply noise across DC-to-GHz frequencies by -40dB (meaning interference is reduced to roughly 1/10,000th of its original strength), all within just 294µm² using only standard core transistors.
key_novelty: Standard-transistor voltage references can now operate at ultra-low 0.8V power levels with 31ppm/°C temperature stability and -40dB power-supply-noise rejection in 294µm² by using charge-pump and switched-capacitor switching instead of traditional BJT or special-structure approaches.
contributions: Sub-1V core-MOS-only voltage reference for advanced nodes
294µm2 area enabling on-die integration with minimal overhead
primary_theme: Ultra-compact sub-1V core-MOS voltage reference with high PSRR
